summary: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): loss of a foot or an eye is compensated at 50 shillings each — exactly 0.50 of the freeman's wergild, placing major limb/eye loss at half a life.
label_raw: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): foot = 50 sh (0.50), eye = 50 sh (0.50)
source_citation: Law of Aethelberht (Kent); Museum Facts https://museumfacts.co.uk/history-of-personal-injury-law-anglo-saxon-wergild/ ; Medievalists.net https://www.medievalists.net/2018/01/anglo-saxon-punishments-price-pinky/

summary: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): the death of a freeman (ceorl) is compensated by a wergild of 100 shillings, the reference life-price (1.0) against which all Kentish body-part prices are scaled.
label_raw: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): freeman (ceorl) wergild = 100 shillings (life reference = 1.0)
source_citation: Law of Aethelberht (Kent, c.600); Museum Facts 'Anglo-Saxon Wergild' https://museumfacts.co.uk/history-of-personal-injury-law-anglo-saxon-wergild/

summary: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): loss of the generative/reproductive organ ('kindling limb') is compensated at 300 shillings = 3x the full freeman wergild — pricing loss of procreative capacity above a single death, signaling heavy weighting of lineage/reproductive future.
label_raw: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): reproductive organ = 300 sh = 3x wergild (above a life)

summary: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): fine-grained body-part gradation — thumb = 20 shillings (0.20), individual fingers 4-11 sh (~0.04-0.11), front tooth = 6 sh (0.06), molar/other tooth = 1 sh (0.01) — with the tooth the cheapest rung at ~0.01 of a life.
label_raw: Law of Aethelberht (Kent): thumb=20sh(0.20), fingers=4-11sh, front tooth=6sh(0.06), molar=1sh(0.01)

summary: Laws of Alfred (Wessex, c.890): independent ~3-centuries-later corroboration in the same tradition — eye = 66 shillings, foot at the knee = 80, great toe = 20, loss of procreative capacity = 80 — notably pricing the genital injury at foot-tier (NOT above a life), showing the 'reproduction > death' weighting was not universal even within one tradition.
label_raw: Laws of Alfred (Wessex): eye=66sh, foot(at knee)=80sh, great toe=20sh, procreative capacity=80sh (foot-tier, not above life)
source_citation: Laws of Alfred (Wessex, c.890); Medievalists.net 'Price of a Pinky' https://www.medievalists.net/2018/01/anglo-saxon-punishments-price-pinky/

summary: Hammurabi SS196-197: destroying the eye or breaking the bone of a social equal (awilum) is punished by talio (in-kind retaliation), not cash — a 1.0 in-kind equivalence of the same injury rather than a compensation price.
label_raw: Code of Hammurabi SS196-197 (eye/bone of an awilum: talio)
source_citation: Code of Hammurabi SS196-197; eHammurabi https://ehammurabi.org/law/196 ; Wikipedia 'Code of Hammurabi'

summary: Hammurabi S198: the eye or bone of a commoner (muskenum) is priced at a fixed compensation of 1 mina of silver (60 shekels) — the cash-priced reference rung for this victim class — rather than talio.
label_raw: Code of Hammurabi S198 (muskenum eye/bone = 1 mina = 60 shekels)
source_citation: Code of Hammurabi S198; eHammurabi https://ehammurabi.org/law/198

summary: Hammurabi S199: injuring a slave's eye or bone is compensated at half the slave's market value, paid to the owner — encoding the slave as chattel so the injury value scales with property price, a separate property-based scale rather than a human life-price.
label_raw: Code of Hammurabi S199 (slave eye/bone = 1/2 chattel market value, paid to owner)
source_citation: Code of Hammurabi S199; eHammurabi https://ehammurabi.org/law/199

summary: Hammurabi SS209-210: causing a free man's daughter to miscarry by striking her is compensated at 10 shekels of silver; if she herself dies, talio applies to the striker's own daughter (life-for-life), with the same act against lower classes priced far lower.
label_raw: Code of Hammurabi SS209-210 (free man's daughter miscarriage = 10 shekels; her death = talio on striker's daughter)
source_citation: Code of Hammurabi SS209-210; eHammurabi assault group https://ehammurabi.org/lch/law-groups/assault

summary: Hammurabi SS200-201: an equal's knocked-out tooth draws talio while a commoner's tooth is compensated at 1/3 mina (20 shekels) — within-code ratio places the commoner's tooth at ~0.33 of the commoner's eye/bone, the cheapest body part priced.
label_raw: Code of Hammurabi SS200-201 (commoner tooth = 1/3 mina = 20 shekels = 0.33 x eye)
source_citation: Code of Hammurabi SS200-201; eHammurabi assault group https://ehammurabi.org/lch/law-groups/assault

summary: Roman Twelve Tables VIII.4: a minor injury/insult (iniuria) is compensated at 25 asses — within-code, 1/12 of a free man's broken bone (300 asses), the lowest priced rung above the talio/bone tiers.
label_raw: Twelve Tables VIII.4 (iniuria = 25 asses = 1/12 of free man's broken bone)

summary: Roman Twelve Tables VIII.2: a maimed/broken limb (membrum ruptum) is the top injury tier, punished by talio in kind unless the parties agree composition — quasi-irreparable, with no fixed cash ceiling.
label_raw: Twelve Tables VIII.2 (membrum ruptum: talio unless composition)
source_citation: Twelve Tables VIII.2; Perseus Dict. of Greek & Roman Antiquities 'Talio' https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.04.0063:alphabetic+letter%3DT:entry%3Dtalio-cn

summary: Roman Twelve Tables VIII.3: a broken bone (os fractum) of a free man is compensated at 300 asses and of a slave at 150 asses — a clean 2:1 free:slave status ratio within the bone tier.
label_raw: Twelve Tables VIII.3 (os fractum: free man = 300 asses, slave = 150 asses; free:slave = 2:1)
source_citation: Twelve Tables VIII.3; Perseus 'Talio'/'Iniuria' https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.04.0063:entry=injuria-cn ; Loeb The Twelve Tables (1938) https://www.loebclassics.com/view/twelve_tables/1938/pb_LCL329.477.xml

summary: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): the galanas (blood-price for the death) of a free man (bonheddig) is 3,780 pence = 63 cows, the reference life-price (1.0) in the two-layer galanas/sarhaed system where galanas = 3 x sarhaed.
label_raw: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): free man galanas = 3,780 pence = 63 cows (life reference = 1.0)
source_citation: Cyfraith Hywel / Galanas; Wikipedia 'Galanas' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galanas ; Wikipedia 'Cyfraith Hywel' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyfraith_Hywel

summary: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): the 'nine limbs of equal value' (two hands, two eyes, two feet, two lips/eyelids, nose) are each compensated at 480 pence ~0.127 of a free man's galanas (~1/8 of a life); all nine sum to ~4,320 pence, exceeding one life — a coherent severity ceiling.
label_raw: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): each of nine equal-value limbs = 480 pence (~0.127 of life); all nine > one life
source_citation: Cyfraith Hywel / Galanas; Wikipedia 'Galanas' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galanas ; Wikipedia 'Cyfraith Hywel' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyfraith_Hywel

summary: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): the base sarhaed (insult/injury price) = galanas / 3 = 1,260 pence, i.e. 0.33 of a free man's life-price — the structural one-third rule linking the dignity/injury layer to the blood-price layer.
label_raw: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): base sarhaed = galanas/3 = 1,260 pence (0.33 of life)

summary: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): distinctive status design — the physical-loss component is egalitarian and fixed regardless of rank (a king's eye = a villein's eye = 480 pence), while only the dignity/insult component (sarhaed) scales with rank (queen's/heir's sarhaed = 1/3 of the king's).
label_raw: Cyfraith Hywel (Wales): body-part value flat across rank (king's eye = villein's eye = 480 pence); only sarhaed status-graded
source_citation: Cyfraith Hywel; Welsh law (EPFL Wikispeedia mirror of Wikipedia) https://dlab.epfl.ch/wikispeedia/wpcd/wp/w/Welsh_law.htm ; Sarah Woodbury 'Laws of Hywel Dda' https://www.sarahwoodbury.com/laws-of-hywel-dda/
